detail: ROOT CAUSE of the turn-3 failure, confirmed and located. Lucius (#4) with Lightning (0x3E, range byte 0x12 = min 1, max 2) EQUIPPED in slot 0 moved to (10,2) and was told: "Attack is unavailable — no enemy is within its weapon range 2-1 of (10,2)." The printed range is 2-1: min greater than max, an empty interval, so no tile can ever satisfy it. src/fe7.ts:609 reads `{ min: b[0] & 0x0f, max: (b[0] >> 4) & 0x0f }` and the comment at src/fe7.ts:52 says "range (hi nibble max, lo min)" — both are backwards. RAM.md is explicit and Confirmed the other way ("+0x19 range, packed — high nibble = min, low nibble = max", settled by the ballista entries 0x34-0x36 reading 0x3A = 3-10), and my own ROM dump of the item table agrees. CONSEQUENCE: fe7_act cannot perform ANY attack at range 2 with a 1-2 weapon — every hand axe, javelin, short spear, light/anima/dark tome decodes to the empty range 2-1. Symmetric weapons (0x11 sword/axe 1-1, 0x22 bow 2-2) are unaffected, which is why this survived until now, and it also explains turn 3: #5's Iron Axe printed "1-1" correctly while both its Hand Axes silently decoded to the empty 2-1, so the union looked like 1-1. fe7_forecast does NOT share the bug — it happily produced a Hand Axe forecast at range 2 — which is why the two tools contradicted each other. Second occurrence of the Wait-fallback: this failure ALSO spent Lucius ("Waited instead") at (10,2). Not fixing mid-run per CLAUDE.md; playing the rest of the chapter melee-only.
wanted: src/fe7.ts:609 -> `{ min: (b[0] >> 4) & 0x0f, max: b[0] & 0x0f }`, and fix the comment at src/fe7.ts:52. Then add a regression check: Hand Axe 0x28 must decode 1-2, Iron Sword 0x01 1-1, Iron Bow 0x2D 2-2, Ballista 0x34 3-10 (the asymmetric one is the whole test). Worth auditing every other consumer of itemRange() for the same assumption, and worth adding the cheap invariant min <= max with a loud throw, since an inverted range fails as "nothing in range" rather than as an error.

detail: Turn 7. I used fe7_act(action:'seize') on Hector at (12,1) purely as a probe — its documented behaviour is to report the menu and press nothing, which makes it the only safe way to see what commands exist. It returned: "the menu holds [0x8b9559c, item, trade, wait]". Three of four named; the first is a bare pointer. So I dumped the table from ROM. It is a clean array: base 0x08b95314, stride 0x24, EXACTLY 27 entries (index 0..26) terminated by an all-zero entry at 0x08b956e0, and every entry carries a name text ID at +0x00 and a description text ID at +0x02 (all 0x81c). index = (ptr - 0x08b95314) / 0x24. Known anchors: idx0 seize (name 0x3f94), idx1 attack (0x3f8c), idx22 item (0x3ec4), idx23 trade (0x3ebc), idx26 wait (0x3ea0). The unnamed entry Hector had is idx18, name text ID 0x3ef4. Given it appeared only with four allies adjacent and sits four slots before Item, alongside idx19/20/21 (0x3ee8/0x3edc/0x3ed0), it is very probably Rescue with Take/Drop/Give around it — but I am NOT asserting that, because "location is not semantics" and I have not tested it by effect. What I can assert: src/fe7.ts:776 MENU_CMD hardcodes 5 of 27 commands, so 22 of the game's own unit actions are invisible to the tool layer and unreachable through it. Notably idx1 and idx2 share the same name ID 0x3f8c and the same +0x04 word, i.e. there are two distinct Attack-family entries — a detail that would matter to any code deriving the Attack index.</detail>
wanted: Decode the +0x00 name text ID through the text decoder the tools already have (the same one that reads 0x0202A5B4 for fe7_unstick's text buffer) and build MENU_CMD from ROM at startup instead of hardcoding 5 pointers — the table is self-terminating, so this is a loop, not a transcription. Then fe7_act can (a) name every entry it reports, which turns "[0x8b9559c, item, trade, wait]" into a usable answer, and (b) offer a generic fe7_act({action:'menu', command:'rescue'|'visit'|'door'|'chest'|...}) that derives the index by pointer the way 'seize' already does, rather than needing a new hand-written action per command. That single change unblocks rescue, trade, visit, door, chest, steal, talk and dance at once.

A wall unit with 37 HP was therefore never safe, and nothing in the tool layer would tell me that. The defend objective makes it strictly worse than a normal map: on a rout map a dead wall unit costs you a unit, here it costs the chapter instantly, because the thing behind the wall has 10 HP and moves on its own.</detail>
